title: Silas and the Signal
premise: Ansel Nystrom, a nonbinary cargo hauler and former insurance investigator, has spent twelve years staying invisible in contested orbits—until gravity flickers system-wide for exactly nine seconds, a phenomenon only they recognize as the signature of a dead experiment their mother helped build. The flicker is a distress signal from the Meridian relay at the edge of dead space, where the fleet's fragile truce is about to expire and both factions will claim whatever answers lie inside. Racing rival salvagers and a fleet auditor who suspects Ansel's identity, Ansel discovers the relay holds their mother's archived consciousness—and proof that the truce was engineered around a weaponized version of her work. In the end, Ansel must choose between destroying the archive to keep everyone safe or broadcasting it and shattering the peace, ultimately sending a partial signal that exposes the corruption while preserving their mother's memory on their own terms.
about_author: Cyrus Reyes is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years aboard research vessels before turning to fiction. They write near-future science fiction about people who fix things no one wants to admit are broken.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Mid-haul through contested orbits, gravity fails for exactly nine seconds; Ansel alone recognizes the waveform pattern from their childhood. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: The Adjuster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter in Ansel's POV, reconstructing their years investigating impossible accidents and the mother whose 'failed' experiment keeps surfacing in claims files. Emotional beat: grief braided with professional detachment cracking open.

chapters.title: Auditor at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Fleet auditor Imara Voss boards Ansel's ship under truce-inspection pretenses, clearly hunting whoever recognized the flicker. Ansel lies badly. The beat is cat-and-mouse tension and the first hint that Voss knows more than she says.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Ansel slips custody and plots a run to the Meridian relay, bartering fuel from an old salvage contact who warns that rival crews are already moving. Beat: reluctant resolve—Ansel chooses the race over hiding.

chapters.title: What the Wreckage Wanted
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She decodes fleet records linking the nine-second flicker to Project Lattice and Ansel's mother, Dr. Ione Nystrom. Torn between duty and suspicion of her own command, she pursues Ansel. Beat: loyalty beginning to rot.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, crossing dead space with failing systems and Voss's ship shadowing them. A near-fatal drift forces an uneasy docking and first honest conversation. Beat: two guarded people discovering a shared enemy.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: They reach the relay and find it occupied by salvagers stripping it under a forged truce waiver. A standoff turns violent; Ansel breaks through to the core archive. Beat: adrenaline giving way to awe at the threshold of the truth.

chapters.title: Mother, Recorded
chapters.summary: Inside the archive, Ansel confronts their mother's preserved consciousness and learns Lattice was repurposed into a gravity weapon the truce was built to conceal. Beat: devastating intimacy—inheritance revealed as both gift and burden.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: Climax. Both fleets converge as the ceasefire clock runs out; Voss must choose between orders and evidence while Ansel fights to control the broadcast array. Beat: sacrifice under fire, power's machinery laid bare.

chapters.title: The Signal That Remained
chapters.summary: Resolution. Ansel broadcasts a partial transmission—corruption exposed, weapon data destroyed, mother's memory kept whole. Voss testifies; the fleets stall rather than fight. Ansel returns to hauling cargo, finally visible. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
